## Phase 2 (Repair) — implemented per the approved plan; RED→GREEN + mutation-verified

Worktree `../aefe-store-usability` off `origin/main` `565e1856bc9d`. Plan-review attestation
re-checked at implementation time and still `certified` (`review-plan --status`:
`verified_at_sha 565e1856…`, `currency_basis file_impact`).

### RED baseline (drove the real public entry point, not a unit stub)

`rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=…)` against three stores, before any code change:

| store shape | before |
|---|---|
| tracker dir present, `reviewbot-ensure-tickets` marker, NO `.git` (the production shape) | `[]` |
| mid-clone: `.git` present, `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` rc **1** | `[]` |
| control: `init_repo` store, zero tickets | `[]` (correct, must stay) |

Confirms the RCA: all three are indistinguishable. (Minor correction to the Phase-1 note —
the probe returns rc **1**, not 128, because `-q` suppresses the error; non-zero either way,
so the predicate is unaffected.)

### Change (exactly the approved four files + test file)

- **new** `src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py` — `store_is_usable(tracker)` = `isdir` AND
  `.git` present AND `git -C <tracker> rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` resolves. Stdlib-only.
  `check=False`, so a clean non-zero rc means "HEAD unresolvable" -> not usable, while an
  `OSError` (git binary missing) PROPAGATES rather than collapsing into a store verdict.
- `src/rebar/_reads.py` — `_tracker` gates on the shared predicate instead of bare `isdir`.
- `src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py` — `_ensure_initialized` calls the same predicate
  (the `os` import became unused and was removed).
- `src/rebar/audit/server.py` — docstring corrected to state that EVERY `store_uninitialized`
  (absent AND present-but-unusable) degrades to an empty index, and the WARNING broadened so
  the present-but-unusable case is logged rather than silently blanked. No behaviour change at
  that layer.

46 added lines across the three edited src files + a 56-line new leaf (mostly rationale
comment) — well inside the `bugfix-size-attestation` threshold, and the bug carries a
certified plan-review attestation regardless. One change, no split needed.

### Write-gate safety, proven rather than asserted

Instrumented `_ensure_initialized` across `init_repo` + `create_ticket` + `comment`: **2**
calls, and at BOTH `git rev-parse HEAD` already resolved and `store_is_usable` was `True`.
The probe is anchored — it asserts the guard was actually exercised, so a zero-call run would
fail rather than pass vacuously. Init's initial commits come from `init_core`, not through the
guarded append path, so widening the write gate to reject a mid-clone store does not break
init or first write.

### Mutation results — 6 seeded, 6 killed

Each production edit reverted individually, targeted tests re-run, **return code checked**
(not output eyeballed), and each seed verified to have actually applied (anchored replaces
with `count == 1` asserts; a no-op seed is reported as `SEED-NOOP`, never as a kill).

| # | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `_reads`: `store_is_usable` -> bare `os.path.isdir` | **killed** — 14 failed |
| M2 | write gate: revert to `isdir` + `.git` | **killed** — 1 failed |
| M3 | predicate: drop the `.git` check | **killed** — 8 failed *(see below)* |
| M4 | predicate: drop the HEAD probe (`return True`) | **killed** — 8 failed |
| M5 | predicate: swallow `OSError` as not-usable | **killed** — 1 failed |
| M6 | audit: revert the warning wording | **killed** — 1 failed |

**M3 initially SURVIVED, and that was a real coverage gap, not a mutation-testing artifact.**
`git -C <dir> rev-parse HEAD` walks UP to the nearest enclosing repository, so the `.git`-exists
check exists precisely to stop an unusable tracker resolving the enclosing CODE repo's HEAD.
My first fixture built the enclosing repo with `git init` and no commit, so ITS head did not
resolve either — the walk-up hazard was never exercised and deleting the check changed nothing.
Fixed by giving the enclosing repo a real commit (the production shape: the tracker sits inside
a normal checkout) and asserting, as a precondition, that git DOES resolve a HEAD by walking up
from the tracker dir. M3 then fails 8 tests.

### Vacuity anchoring (this bug is literally about vacuous results)

- Every success-asserting test seeds a real ticket and asserts it comes BACK, so `[]` cannot
  satisfy it. The `.env-id` test asserts the seeded id specifically.
- The predicate test asserts `True` for usable shapes as well as `False` for unusable ones, so
  an always-`False` predicate fails it.
- The write-gate test asserts the initialized store is ACCEPTED as well as the mid-clone
  REJECTED, so an always-raising guard fails it.
- The `OSError` test first asserts the store IS usable without the fault injected, so the raise
  is attributable to the injected `OSError` and not to the store's shape.
- **The audit test was itself vacuous on first write and I caught it**: `assert caplog.records`
  passed against the UNFIXED code because it was matching an unrelated
  `REBAR_NO_SYNC`-deprecation warning from `rebar.config`. Now scoped to
  `r.name == "rebar.audit.server"` and to a message naming the unusable case; it fails RED as
  it should.

### Gates

`make lint` rc=0 · `make typecheck` rc=0 (mypy, 685 files) ·
`check_complexity_baseline.py --check` `new=0 increased=0` ·
`check_raw_git_writes.py` rc=0 (the probe is a READ verb and carries a `raw-git-ok` marker) ·
target file 30/30 pass. Full `make test` running.

### Discovered work (filed + linked `discovered_from`)

- `contained-coherent-tick` (`fe07-314a-2465-40db`) — the approved plan's out-of-scope parity
  item: `reads_cli.py:340,384` still gate on bare `os.path.isdir`, so the CLI now DISAGREES
  with library/MCP on a broken store (before this fix they agreed, both wrong).
- `gangrene-dissected-nymph` (`d582-e941-96b6-41a8`) — measured, and it contradicts the plan's
  assumption. The plan reasoned the probe is negligible because reads already spawn git; but
  `_fresh` is throttled to <=1/min, so most reads spawn none today and the predicate adds an
  **unthrottled** one. Measured on a 25-ticket store: `list_tickets` 22.7ms with the predicate
  vs 5.6ms with it neutralized — **17.1ms, +305%**. Absolute cost is one git startup and log
  reduction dominates on the production tracker, so I shipped the approved design rather than
  improvise a cache (a cached "usable" verdict is exactly this bug's staleness hazard) or
  hand-roll ref resolution. Recorded for a deliberate decision instead of silently absorbed.
